cells.tense: Right now you can give what's fair and take what's fair without keeping score.
cells.act: protect what was won by the ending
cells.ask: Pick something you've already settled — a debt, a favour, a split — and go a whole season without reopening it. Change nothing. Let it keep working while you're elsewhere.
cells.core:
You know how to give and take in kind, and it doesn't take arithmetic anymore. A call you made earlier is holding, and you're letting it. People get the plain version of you, and nobody has to ask twice. What you hand over matches what comes back closely enough that you can stop watching it.

There's something this ease is free to feed next. Pick one exchange you've already settled — a debt, a favour, a split of something — and go a whole season without reopening it. Don't square it up further, don't improve it. Let what you decided keep working while you go do other things. Nothing needs tending for it to hold, and you'll find that out by leaving it.
cells.sheetLine: What you settled is holding. Leave it where it is.
cells.place: where you say this, not that

cells.tense: In the exchanges coming up, you will be paying in before anyone has asked.
cells.act: persist on your own reserves through the pressure
cells.ask: This week, don't bring in help or cover. Carry your own load to the end, and let finishing be enough.
cells.core:
Where you trade with people, you get there first with the favour, the fix, the extra, and the ledger in your head stays open because the next entry is already in it. It reads as generosity from outside. From inside it's bracing — you're trying to stay in front of a reckoning that may not come. The giving has stopped being an offer and become a way of standing guard.

This week, don't bring in help or cover. Carry your own load to the end, and let finishing be enough. Something gets clearer when nobody owes you. What's left after that is what you can actually give, and you'll know the size of it by what it costs.
cells.sheetLine: You pay in early so the debt can't be called.

cells.tense: By the time that exchange got settled, you had already turned toward the door.
cells.act: sort what matters from what does not, carefully
cells.ask: Look at what you're still carrying for others — a task, a worry, an apology owed — and set down whichever one isn't yours. Keep the rest.
cells.core:
At its best this looks like level exchange you can read in a moment without checking. You hand over what's yours to hand over, take what comes back, and neither costs you a night of arithmetic. That's what it does when it's running.

What's happening instead is that you still do the things. Doing plenty and being at the table are two different facts, and the second has gone quiet. What you hold up doesn't match what comes back, and you've stopped bringing that up. Look at what you're still carrying for others — a task, a worry, or an apology owed — and set down whichever one isn't yours. Keep the rest. One clear line tells you where the next one belongs.
cells.sheetLine: You still do the things. You're not at the table.

cells.tense: Fairness moves through you in real time and you have not been putting your name on it.
cells.act: hold two true things without declaring either
cells.ask: When you feel a thing isn't fair and also why it might be, hold both for a day. Don't commit to one. Let the two sit next to each other.
cells.core:
You read a room's fairness fast, faster than you say, and the read tends to hold. It shows in what you hand over before anyone asks and what you quietly stop handing over. A direction is being picked in those moments. The picking has been filed under manners.

When you feel a thing isn't fair and also why it might be, hold both for a day. Don't commit to one, don't settle it. Let the two sit next to each other and see what the day does to them. What you know before you speak is yours, and it lands better when you've held it a moment.
cells.sheetLine: You read what's fair fast. Hold both sides a day.
cells.place: where you say this, not that
